title: Phasmophobia's next update lets you tell ghosts what to do, and it has a release date

content:
Phasmophobia's next major update will let ghost hunters ask spirits to interact with doors, switches and nearby objects. Kinetic Games has confirmed that the free Resonance update arrives on November 24 across the game's current platforms.

There is much more than a new list of things to shout into a microphone. The update introduces dowsing rods for finding the Bone, changes the sound sensor and moves the game to Unity 6, alongside lighting improvements and bug fixes.

VR players are included in those changes. Kinetic has also explained how the new commands will work if you use text-based voice recognition, so you do not have to rely on a microphone to try them.

A promotional screenshot from Phasmophobia. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

Ghost hunters can ask for more specific signs

In its development preview, Kinetic says the expanded recognition system will let players ask ghosts to interact with nearby doors and switches, throw objects or give a sign of their presence. The journal will list the usable phrases.

Those options will be available through text recognition as well. For VR players using text mode, the developer says the commands will be accessible on the sanity watch.

That should make it easier to know what you can actually ask, instead of guessing through an investigation. Of course, having a new command is not a guarantee that a ghost will cooperate.

An existing-game screenshot; Kinetic says Resonance will improve lighting. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

Dowsing rods and a redesigned sound sensor are on the way

The new dowsing rods are intended to help locate the Bone, particularly on large maps such as Brownstone High School. Tier 1 points towards a general direction, while the higher tier can narrow the location down to a floor.

Kinetic is also reworking the sound sensor's map interface. It says icons will distinguish ongoing sounds from one-off noises, and players will be able to use movement speed as one clue when identifying a ghost. The sensor only identifies sounds on the same floor as the player.

There is also a custom random map pool: players can choose which locations the game selects from and use shortcuts for small, medium or large maps.

Full patch notes are expected when Resonance launches. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

Unity 6 brings lighting changes and a VR setting

Kinetic says the engine transition is intended to improve stability and performance, and it expects to address crashes and other bugs. Those are the developer's expectations; the studio says it can judge the performance change properly once players have the update.

Resonance also adds lighting changes, new quality settings and an eye-adaptation option for VR. The studio's release-date announcement says full patch notes will arrive when the update launches.

If you are considering playing the PC version in VR, the Meta Quest 3 can connect to a compatible gaming PC for PC VR. Phasmophobia is a separate purchase and does not run as a native standalone Quest game; a headset is optional for the standard PC version.

For context, MIXED previously covered the Crimson Eye event. Resonance is a separate update, and Kinetic has not included the later character-cosmetics refresh in its launch plans.
